text:
Ana: Quick sync — mapping patches vs polish. Proposing 60/40 bug-first for the next mini-iteration (2 weeks). Rationale: 3 high-severity customer regressions (ACME, Kiva, OmniPay) + NPS signals. See tickets: #8421, #8479, #8502. Thoughts?

Tom: 60/40 sounds right. Can we scope which 'polish' items are non-blocking? I'd rather defer any UX tweaks that don't impact conversion.

Priya: Agree. Also flagging that bug #8479 affects streaming latency on Dedicated — that's on the SLA radar. If we don't fix, we might need an interim rollback.

Jules: +1. Can we do an owner map? Suggest pairing one eng for each high bug + one for polish lead. That keeps momentum.

Matt: I'll own #8421 (ACME model mismatch). ETA 3d for root cause if we can get reproducer from CS.

Leah: sending reproducer now, and customer is ok with a patch deploy mid-week. Also, customer-facing note ok to share.

Ana: Ok — new plan: Week1 = triage + patch for high-severity (3 bugs). Week2 = implement 2 highest-priority polishes that unblock conversions + regression test. We'll freeze any low-priority UX tweaks to next cycle. @Tom @Jules can you confirm?

Tom: Confirmed. Also please add 'rollback playbook' step for the streaming fix.

Jules: I'll set up a 30m grooming tomorrow 10:30 to map tasks and owners. Agenda: repro status, test coverage, deploy window, canary criteria.

deploy-bot: Note: scheduled canary slot opens wed 02:00-04:00 UTC. Please tag PRs with 'canary-wed'

Ana: Perfect. I'll update the iteration board and tag all tickets. Linking the patch mapping doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/patch-mapping/3712345678 (draft).

Priya: One ask — include acceptance criteria for each polish item; we need measurable metrics (CTR, error rate) to avoid scope creep.

Tom: ACK. Adding: acceptance criteria + perf budget per ticket.

Ana: Thanks all. If no objections by EOD, I'll lock iteration and send calendar invites for grooming and daily stand for the mini-iteration. :handshake:
